title: Hermetica, Vol. 1
author: Walter Scott (ed)
description: Hermetica, Volume 1, edited with English translation and notes by Walter Scott (Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1924), subtitled 'The ancient Greek and Latin writings which contain religious or philosophic teachings ascribed to Hermes Trismegistus'. This volume contains Scott's introduction on the Hermetic literature and its manuscripts, together with the Greek and Latin texts and facing translations of the Corpus Hermeticum (including the Poimandres, the Key, the Crater, the discourse on rebirth and others) and the Latin Asclepius, with its famous lament for Egypt and passage on the animation of statues. Scott's edition is learned but notorious for heavy emendation and rearrangement of the texts, so later scholars use it with caution. It nonetheless remains a major English resource on Hermetic theology: the divine Mind, the creation of the cosmos and humanity, the soul's ascent and rebirth, and gnosis of God.
